reason: Join the upper digestive tract to the colon to prepare the lower body; the picture shows where they meet.
expectation: I expect a continuous digestive tract that can later fit into the lower body.

alternatives.reason: Placing the eye in the head is also a clear goal, but I chose to start with the digestive tract.

effect: The small intestine and colon now form a continuous digestive tract, ready to place in the lower body.
reaction: The separate food and blood arrows make their connection clearer.
reason: Fit the completed digestive tract into its marked lower-body space.
expectation: I expect the digestive tract to sit inside the lower body, with room still available for the urinary organs.

effect: The digestive tract is in the abdomen, with its food pipe leading toward the chest and throat.
reaction: Seeing where the colon and small intestine fit together is helpful.
reason: Complete the lower body by fitting the urinary organs into their marked space.
expectation: I expect the kidneys, ureters and bladder to fit alongside the digestive tract.

effect: The lower body now contains both the digestive tract and urinary organs, with separate outlets.
reason: Start preparing the head by placing the eye and its optic nerve.
expectation: I expect the eye to fit into the head with its nerve leading toward the brain.

alternatives.reason: The ears also belong in the head, but I chose the eye first.

effect: The eye is in its socket, with its optic nerve leading into the existing brain.
reaction: The supplied second eye makes the head model feel complete without duplicating the studied eye.
reason: Add the ears to finish preparing the head's sense organs.
expectation: I expect the ears to fit into the head with their hearing and balance nerves leading toward the brain.

effect: The head now has the eye and ears, with their nerves connected toward the brain.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the hearing and balance parts remain together.
reason: Attach the arm to the chest as part of preparing the body.
expectation: I expect the arm assembly to join the chest at the shoulder, keeping its muscles and bones intact.

alternatives.reason: The lymph network also belongs with the chest, but I chose the visible arm connection first.

effect: The arm is attached at the shoulder, with its blood vessels and nerves meeting the chest routes.
reaction: It is useful to see the arm connect to more than just the skeleton.
reason: Add the lymph drainage network to continue preparing the chest; its return route connects to a neck vein.
expectation: I expect the lymph vessels to join the chest and connect to the blood route near the neck.

alternatives.reason: The repaired skin segment also needs fitting, but I want to finish the chest first.

effect: The lymph network is aligned with the chest's existing neck vein, completing preparation of the chest and lower body.
reaction: The shared vein connection is clear.
reason: Join the prepared lower body and chest before fitting the skin, as the chapter directs.
expectation: I expect the lower body to connect beneath the diaphragm, keeping its organs and the chest structures in place.

alternatives.reason: The repaired segment also needs to go into the skin covering, but I want to join the body regions first.

effect: The chest and lower body are joined, and the open back channel is ready for the spine.
reaction: The diaphragm makes the division between chest and abdomen clear.
reason: Join the head and spine to the trunk before fitting the skin last.
expectation: I expect the spine to fit into the back channel and the head to join the trunk, with the existing routes aligned.

alternatives.reason: The repaired skin segment also needs fitting, but I want to join the body regions first.

effect: The head and spine are joined to the trunk, with nerves and blood routes reaching the body's regions.
reaction: Seeing the same muscle depend on both nerves and blood ties earlier chapters together.
reason: Fit the repaired segment into the skin covering; it is the only available combination and prepares the covering for the body.
expectation: I expect the repaired segment to fill the matching opening in the covering.

effect: The repaired segment fills its original opening, and the covering is ready to fit over the body.
reaction: The small scar makes the earlier repair visible without replacing the surrounding skin.
reason: Fit the prepared skin covering onto the body; this is the only available combination and completes the current goal.
expectation: I expect the covering to fit over the body, with the repaired segment remaining at its original location.

effect: The skin covering completes the body while leaving a cutaway showing how the parts remain connected and active.
reaction: The scar and cutaway make the finished model feel connected to the earlier work.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the head and spine to the trunk was most worthwhile because it brought nerves and blood supply together and showed that muscles need both.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the digestive tract and urinary organs into named spaces was clear but fairly predictable; the choices mostly followed the labeled slots.

surprise.text: The diaphragm separates the chest from the abdomen, while nerves, blood vessels and the food pipe still cross between them through their own routes.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary. Some fittings were guided by named spaces rather than requiring me to figure out compatibility.

continue.text: I probably would not continue immediately. The completed body provides a satisfying endpoint, though seeing the separate systems connect was interesting.
